transcript.content: Good day. What brings you in today?

I came in because I just… I can’t stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like at work, if something slips or even if it’s not really my department, I feel like I’m a bad employee. And then at home, with the house, I keep thinking I don’t deserve it, like I’m a bad homeowner and I’m going to lose everything I worked for.

Sorry, I know that’s not very organized. It’s just been sitting on me all the time.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself even when things aren’t really your fault, or does this feeling usually happen only in situations where something actually went wrong?

It’s… not only when something actually goes wrong. I mean, if something goes wrong, definitely, I take it on like it proves I’m a bad employee or like I don’t deserve my house, which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud.

But even when it’s not really my fault, I still feel like I should’ve prevented it somehow. Like there’s always some angle where I could’ve done better. And then I get stuck on it—like I’m the reason things fall apart.

Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t an immediate problem, or does this kind of thinking usually only happen in specific situations related to work or home?

It kind of spreads out, I think. Work and the house are the big ones, because they feel like proof, you know? Like if I make a mistake at work, I’m a bad employee, and if something is wrong at home, I’m a bad homeowner and I don’t deserve to keep what I worked for.

But then it turns into this whole… I don’t know, like a general feeling that everything that goes wrong is somehow my fault. Even small things. I’ll start thinking I should’ve done more, or seen it coming, and then I get stuck there.
Do you find yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, even when you’re not thinking about work or home problems?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not just when I’m spiraling about work or the house. I used to be the person who planned brunches, like I’d make the group chat and pick the place, and I used to paint in the spare room—well, I bought all these little organizers for the brushes, which was probably unnecessary, but I liked it.

And hiking too, I used to actually look forward to that. Networking events, even, which sounds weird because most people hate those, but I used to sign up and feel like it was part of building something.

Now all of that just feels like… tasks. Like I’m pretending to care about them because I remember I’m supposed to care. It’s hard to explain, but the interest isn’t really there the way it used to be.
Have you noticed that your mood is low most of the day, nearly every day, even when there isn’t a specific reason for it?

Yeah… most days, honestly. It’s been going on a long time—like, I tried to count it because at first I thought maybe it was just a bad quarter at work, you know, like when everything piles up and you tell yourself it’ll pass after the next deadline.

But it didn’t really lift. The low mood and not being interested in things… that’s been there for about two years and a month now. I know that sounds oddly specific, but I’ve sort of tracked it around seasons and birthdays and all that.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally taxing?

I don’t know if I’d call it fatigue exactly. I mean, I get tired, but everybody gets tired, right? Sometimes I’ll sit down after work and it’s like… hard to get back up, but then I start thinking maybe that’s just because I didn’t eat a real lunch or because my chair at the office is terrible.

Actually, I’ve been meaning to fix that chair situation because the adjustable lever sticks, and I keep telling myself I should put in a facilities request, but then it feels like such a small thing to bother someone about.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I haven’t really tracked my energy the way I’ve tracked my mood.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like painting or hiking, no longer give you any sense of pleasure or satisfaction, even when you make yourself do them?

Yeah… that’s probably the best way to put it. Like, I can still technically do them. I can sit in the spare room with the paints out, or I can agree to a hike, but it feels more like I’m completing an obligation than enjoying it.

I used to plan brunches and get weirdly excited about picking the place, and I’d sign up for networking events like they mattered. Now it’s like I’m going through the motions because I remember that I used to be that person. It doesn’t really give me that… satisfaction anymore.
Would you say that your low mood is present most of the day, nearly every day, even when there isn’t a specific reason for it?

Yeah… I mean, I think I already kind of said this, but it’s been there most days. The low mood and the not really caring about things the way I used to… that’s been going on for about two years and one month.

I only remember it that clearly because I kept thinking it would pass after, like, a busy season or after things settled down, but then the months just kept adding up.
Do you find that you no longer feel any sense of enjoyment or pleasure in activities, even ones that used to make you happy or that you looked forward to?

Yeah… I think so. I know I kind of already said it, but it’s like those things are still there, technically. I used to be the person who planned brunches and got excited about the menu, or I’d paint in the spare room and lose track of time, or go hiking and feel better afterward.

Now it feels like I’m doing the outline of those things. Like I’m pretending to care because I remember that I used to care. Even networking events, which sounds ridiculous to miss enjoying, but I used to feel motivated by them. Now they just feel like tasks on a list.
Would you say that you no longer feel any enjoyment or interest in activities, even ones you used to really look forward to?

Yeah, I mean… yes. I know I’m kind of repeating myself, but that’s exactly it. I used to plan brunches like it was this whole little project, and I’d paint in the spare room, or go hiking, or sign up for networking events because I actually cared about them.

Now I still do some of it sometimes, but it feels like checking off a box. Like I’m pretending to be interested because I remember that I used to be. It’s not really enjoyment anymore.
Would you say that your mood is often sad, empty, or hopeless, even when you’re not thinking about specific things that might have gone wrong?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that from, like, having an actual reason. Because my brain can always find something, you know? Work, or money, or how I’m supposed to be further along than I am… and then I’ll realize I’ve been sitting there with that heavy feeling before I even picked a reason.

So… maybe? I don’t know. “Hopeless” feels like a big word. Empty, maybe. Sad sometimes. But it’s hard for me to say it’s for no reason, because I always end up attaching it to something after the fact.
Can you recall a time in the past when you felt genuine pleasure or joy while painting or hiking, and how does that compare to how you feel doing those same activities now?

Yeah… I can remember it. Like with painting, I used to set up in the spare room and it would turn into this whole thing—I’d put music on, make coffee, lose track of time. And hiking too, I’d actually look forward to it, like planning the trail and what snacks to bring, which is silly but I cared.

Now I can still do those things sometimes, but it feels… flat. Like I’m going through the motions because I know they’re supposed to be good for me, or because I used to like them. It’s kind of like how I used to plan brunches or sign up for networking events and feel excited or motivated, and now all of that just feels like tasks I’m pretending to care about.
Would you say that you no longer feel any enjoyment or interest in activities, even ones you used to really look forward to?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’ve said it a few times, but it’s like those things are still technically there in my life. I’ll still think, “Oh, I should paint,” or “I should go hike,” or someone will mention brunch and I remember I used to be the one picking the place and making it into this whole event.

But now it’s like… I’m doing an impression of myself. Like I’m pretending to care because I know I used to care. Even networking events—I used to get kind of energized by them, which sounds weird, but now it just feels like another task on a list.
